variants.prompt:
Use case: productivity-visual.
Asset type: one SINGLE 16:9 landscape pitch slide proposal, 1920x1080, crisp typographic editorial design, full bleed slide only, no device, no mockup perspective, no outer canvas. The intended audience is a hackathon jury and investors viewing this ONE slide on stage.
The real product vision: operational intelligence for large multi-site materials businesses. Connect industry signals to the company's own ERP/WMS/CRM facts, investigate relevance, calculate admissible alternatives, preserve human approval, and record decisions. Timber and building materials in France are the first market. Risk and opportunity are business impact types. This is a design proposal. Do not imply that the larger industrial portfolio or commercial opportunity workflow is already integrated.
All authored text MUST be in ENGLISH, clean, short, precisely spelled. Use one refined sans-serif font family with bold/regular hierarchy similar to Inter. Strong whitespace and excellent alignment. All important body text readable at presentation scale. No em dashes. No statistics, percentages, savings, customer logos, fake traction, funding, QR codes, invented URL, stock photography of an actual incident, or grandiose claims. There is no received company brand. Use the small descriptor OPERATIONAL INTELLIGENCE instead of inventing a company name.
Exact copy and required content, keep concise and use this wording:
Main headline: "Turn market changes into company decisions"
Subtitle: "Connect industry signals with your stock, sites and customer commitments."
Product/data visual labels:
"Industry signals" with "News, public data, sector sources"
"Company context" with "ERP / WMS / CRM"
"Stock, orders, customers"
"Agent + business tools" with "Investigate. Calculate. Reassess."
"Human decision" with "Protect commitments" and "Qualify opportunities"
The diagram must show industry signals AND company context informing the agent and business tools, which produce a human-reviewed decision. Depict two intents, risk protection and opportunity qualification, through discreet text and semantic accent colors, without showing either as automatically executed.
Three compact audience/market text areas:
"WHO" / "Operations and procurement teams" / "Starting with French timber and materials"
"WHY NOW" / "Agents can investigate across fragmented sources"
"FIRST USERS" / "Plan: founder introductions to materials businesses"
One compact proof band, use exactly:
"PROTOTYPE EVIDENCE"
"Real model + tools. Approved decision read back in Aiven PostgreSQL."
"Synthetic business data. Measured benchmark pending."
A tiny but visible footer: "Pitch design proposal. Opportunity workflow in development."
Keep all of this content readable, but make the diagram convey the product so this is not a wall of text. No evidence is fabricated. The word A, B, or C is just a small unambiguous direction badge in the top right, not part of the product name.

Direction A, visibly label "A" in the top-right. White/off-white background, deep navy typography, restrained petrol teal accents from the product UI (#155b66), pale grey rules, tiny amber/coral risk accent. A premium Swiss editorial composition: expansive headline across the upper left, graceful custom vector-like diagram across the middle. At the left of the diagram, a few elegant document/source sheets and a small warehouse/order ledger converge as two independent inputs into a precise central agent/calculation motif, then one sober decision document on the right. Extremely clean flat line illustration, never floating rounded-card wallpaper. Use only 3 or 4 subtle surfaces if needed. Under the diagram, align WHO / WHY NOW / FIRST USERS in a single elegant row, then the compact proof band. Main visual around half the canvas. Clear distinction between sector signal and company context. A sophisticated venture pitch aesthetic with generous negative space.

Direction B, visibly label "B" in top-right. Deep navy almost-black background, off-white text, petrol/cyan fine-line details, restrained amber for risks and pale mint for opportunities, no neon glow or 3D robot aesthetic. Make a bold, stage-readable system composition: headline top spanning 70% of slide, then a wide beautifully spaced network of actual data relationships, source documents and company site/order nodes on the left, purposeful agent + calculation hub in the center, a large clean decision record on the right. Connections are sparse, straight or orthogonal, clearly directional through composition. Show human review as a small tasteful person/check motif, not an autonomous purchase. Integrate all labels naturally. Footer area holds three open columns WHO / WHY NOW / FIRST USERS and the proof strip. Elegant technical editorial design, not a screenshot of a dashboard and not a grid of equal boxes.

Direction C, visibly label "C" in top-right. Luminous white background, dark ink typography, petrol teal, light grey, a restrained warm amber signal accent. Create a materially different, product-story pitch composition. The main headline dominates the left third with unusually strong typographic scale. Center and right feature a large carefully composed illustrative cutaway of a multi-site materials operation: warehouse structures, timber/panels, a construction project silhouette, trucks represented minimally. Make this feel like refined architectural axonometric editorial artwork with subtle volume, not cartoon clipart or a photograph. Overlay just a few elegant explanatory callouts for Industry signals and Company context feeding Agent + business tools, leading to Human decision. Keep the physical illustration subordinate enough that every required phrase stays legible. The two human decision intents are small connected annotations. Put WHO / WHY NOW / FIRST USERS in an open lower-third layout and the exact proof text below a thin rule. Design remains one concise serious investor slide, never a brochure or crowded infographic.
